metadata.title: Momentum Survives, Kinetic Energy Does Not
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: Two blocks collide and stick together. What is conserved, and what is lost?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: A two kilogram block slides at four meters per second toward an identical block at rest. When they collide, they stick together. One quantity survives the collision perfectly. Another does not.
beats.new_visual_element: On a black baseline, a vermilion 2 kg block with velocity arrow v₁ = 4 m/s moves toward a teal 2 kg block at rest.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: two blocks on a track, one moving, one at rest

beats.narration_text: On contact, the two blocks become a single four kilogram object, moving at two meters per second: slower than the first block was moving, but faster than the second.
beats.new_visual_element: The blocks touch; a brief gold impact burst; the pair transforms into one merged 4 kg block, and the velocity arrow transforms into v_f = 2 m/s.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: one merged block moving at v_f = 2 m/s

beats.narration_text: Compare the total momentum. Before the collision, it is two kilograms times four meters per second, eight kilogram meters per second. After, it is four kilograms times two meters per second, still eight. Momentum is conserved exactly.
beats.new_visual_element: A bar chart below the track: momentum before, 8 kg·m/s; a second bar, momentum after, grows to exactly the same height. Equation beneath: m₁v₁ = (m₁ + m₂)v_f.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: merged block above; equal momentum bars and the momentum equation below

beats.narration_text: Now compare kinetic energy. Before, one half times two kilograms times four squared gives sixteen joules. After, one half times four kilograms times two squared gives only eight. Half of the kinetic energy has become deformation of the blocks, heat, and sound.
beats.new_visual_element: Beside the momentum bars, kinetic energy bars: before 16 J; the after bar shrinks from 16 J to 8 J with a counting label, and the lost top half peels off as a grey hatched block labeled heat, deformation, sound.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: equal momentum bars beside unequal kinetic energy bars with the hatched lost portion

beats.narration_text: In every collision between two objects free of external forces, momentum is conserved. When the objects stick together, the loss of kinetic energy is the greatest it can be, and the collision is called perfectly inelastic.
beats.new_visual_element: Labels CONSERVED under the momentum bars and NOT CONSERVED under the kinetic energy bars; title: perfectly inelastic: objects stick, kinetic energy is lost, momentum is not.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: merged block, both bar pairs with verdict labels, summary line
